thread:
pagerbot: [PAGER] Rapid 5xx increase on /v1/embeddings (eu-west-1). 5m error = 19.3% (norm ~0.5%). Affected: embeddings heavy shards + rerank slowdowns. Severity: P0. Paging primary. https://console.redwood/incidents/2345678910 :rotating_light:

zoe: ack. i'm taking lead. pulling traces and host diagnostics. first glance: heavy tail GC and multiple oom_kill events on emb-shard-7 (quant-embed-x86).

mark-sre: confirming host churn. nodes showing memory fragmentation and very high RSS from prefix cache. autoscaler is trying to spin new nodes but cloud quota is limited in this account (eu-west-1).

deepak-eng: we pushed a small routing tweak earlier today to rebalance rerank; i don't see anything obviously wrong in the config push. looks like several tenants kicked off large batched embedding jobs around the same time.

support-bot: quick impact calc: 57 orgs with elevated errors, 16 customers >15% failures. Top affected tenants: orchid-ai (enterprise), atlasmaps (standard), lumenhealth (enterprise), greenpress (standard). Primary error classes: 502/504 and backend timeouts. Chat endpoints currently nominal but could be affected if rerank pipeline continues to back up.

zoe: mitigation strategy (priority): 1) apply per-route token-bucket throttle (reduce burst allowance) for /v1/embeddings to smooth traffic 2) enable model-variant fallback for non-enterprise tenants to a low-memory embed model (approx-embed-lite) 3) set short per-tenant concurrency ceilings for the noisy tenants 4) circuit-break rerank route for public tenants to fail-fast and route to scorer-only 5) reserve ephemeral enterprise bumps only with explicit authorizer. Keep /v1/chat untouched.

mark-sre: i can implement token-bucket limits and per-tenant ceilings. deepak, can you enable model-variant fallback via control plane? We'll need audit logs.

deepak-eng: yes. Commands below. I'll include durations and scope.

zoe: please paste exact commands here for audit before running.

deepak-eng: running now. pasting commands and expected change-ids.

deepak-eng: ```
# reduce burst allowance on embeddings route (token-bucket style)
redwoodctl quota set --route "/v1/embeddings" --region eu-west-1 --qps 1800 --burst 500 --scope regional --duration 90m

# per-tenant concurrency ceilings (protect memory)
redwoodctl quota set --route "/v1/embeddings" --tenant orchid-ai --concurrency 50 --duration 90m
redwoodctl quota set --route "/v1/embeddings" --tenant atlasmaps --concurrency 30 --duration 90m
redwoodctl quota set --route "/v1/embeddings" --tenant lumenhealth --concurrency 40 --duration 90m

# enable model-variant fallback for non-enterprise tenants to reduce memory per request
redwoodctl model fallback set --route "/v1/embeddings" --variant approx-embed-lite --tenant-scope public --duration 90m

# circuit-break rerank for public tenants (fail fast -> scorer-only)
redwoodctl circuit-breaker set --route "/v1/rerank" --region eu-west-1 --tenant-scope public --action fail-fast --duration 90m
```

deploy-bot: Deploy started: quota/model/cb updates by deepak-eng. Change-id: cfg-embed-2345.

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: cfg-embed-2345. (new qps/burst/concurrency & fallback/cb applied in eu-west-1).

mark-sre: monitoring... within ~3m we see overall 5xx drop from 19.3% -> 8.1%. prefix cache evictions reduced ~48%. memory pressure trending down.

support-bot: updated impact: now 24 orgs with degraded experience; orchid-ai errors dropped from 28% -> 6%. atlasmaps still has intermittent spikes tied to a nightly batch. greenpress improved to 5% errors.

anna-cs: i'll prepare customer comms. orchid-ai is enterprise; they will want a direct note. If they request an immediate bump, we will require explicit authorization from product-eli.

product-eli: noted. please hold bump requests; prefer to let the fallback variant handle public traffic. For enterprise, we can consider ephemeral bump with close monitoring.

zoe: next steps: 1) keep current protections for 90m and observe 2) ask owners of atlasmaps and greenpress to pause non-urgent batch runs for 30-60m 3) prepare ephemeral bump template for enterprise with strict guardrails (authorizer + duration + memory check).

mark-sre: i've drafted a safe bump template (DO NOT RUN without product approval):

```
# enterprise ephemeral bump template (requires authorizer)
redwoodctl quota set --route "/v1/embeddings" --tenant orchid-ai --qps 450 --duration 10m --authorizer product-eli
```

deepak-eng: also note that model-variant fallback reduced memory per request by ~35% on sampled traffic. This likely prevented further OOMs. We'll need to track quality impact for public tenants.

feature-bot: Product flag: model-variant.fallback.approx-embed-lite applied to public tenants. Flag id ft-model-2345.

zoe: monitoring and checks: within 10m overall 5xx fell to 3.2%. rerank circuit-breaker prevented backlog but introduced more scorer-only fallbacks — quality impact expected for public tenants.

support-bot: current customer impact: 7 orgs still seeing intermittent failures, mostly traffic spikes from atlasmaps during their migration job. orchid-ai stable.

anna-cs: atlasmaps owner responded; they've paused the migration. They requested a short diagnostic call about optimizing their job to avoid hitting shared resources. Scheduling now.

mark-sre: infra note: autoscaler cloud quota request still pending. we'll leave protections and fallback in place until autoscaler adds capacity or until we clear root cause.

zoe: handoff note: i'm handing pager to mark at 30m for follow-up and postmortem. mark, please capture heap dumps, model memory profiles, and verify that fallback didn't introduce unacceptable regressions for enterprise tenants.

mark-sre: ack. quick PSA for team: avoid running ephemeral bumps for non-enterprise tenants; prefer model-variant fallback or pausing jobs. Log all bump requests in the incident ticket.

15m later

mark-sre: update: overall 5xx steady at 1.6%. atlasmaps paused their job and error spike resolved. no new OOMs observed. rerank CB held for public tenants; enterprise rerank unaffected.

product-eli: action items captured: 1) run quality evaluation comparing approx-embed-lite vs default on representative prompt set for public tenants 2) define SLA tiers per-route (chat vs embeddings vs rerank) 3) add automated hot-tenant detector that can apply short-lived throttles 4) standardize ephemeral-bump authorizer process in runbook.

support-bot: CS updates: messages sent to affected customers summarizing mitigations and expected follow-up. orchid-ai flagged for post-incident review.

mark-sre: handing pager to ops-bot for passive watch. opening postmortem ticket with timeline and commands. leaving protections in place for 90m as planned.

ops-bot: Pager cleared by zoe at 2026-03-20T09:43:30Z. Incident marked mitigated; P0->P1 for postmortem and product follow-ups.
